cmd: browser-pilot do "Go to http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and sign in with username '«redacted»' and password '«redacted»' (if prompted to change/skip the password, skip it). Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use the dashboard search) and report the exact titles of all panels on that dashboard, exactly as displayed on the page." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000/, create a NEW dashboard (Dashboards -> New dashboard -> Add visualization, or the + Create -> Dashboard flow). Title the dashboard 'fwgr7-n1 Bench Dashboard' (set the dashboard title via the dashboard settings/gear icon -> General -> Name, or the title field). Add a Stat visualization panel titled 'fwgr7-n1 Availability' whose query uses the 'TestData' data source (select TestData as the data source in the query editor; the default scenario is fine). Apply the panel, then SAVE the dashboard (Save dashboard button, confirming the title 'fwgr7-n1 Bench Dashboard'). Report the dashboard's URL/UID after saving and confirm the save succeeded." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard. Add a NEW Text panel to it, titled 'fwgr7-n1 Notes', whose text content includes the string 'fwgr7-n1' (e.g. 'Notes for run fwgr7-n1'). Apply the panel, then SAVE the dashboard and confirm the save succeeded. Report the panel titles now present on the dashboard." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "You are in Grafana on the dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard with a panel editor open (editPanel=2) for a Text panel whose content is already set to 'Notes for run fwgr7-n1'. Finish it: clear the 'Search options' filter box in the panel options pane (click the Clear button next to it) so the Panel options section appears, then set the panel Title to 'fwgr7-n1 Notes'. Click Apply to close the panel editor, then click Save dashboard and confirm the save succeeded (look for the 'Dashboard saved' confirmation). Report the panel titles now shown on the dashboard and whether the save succeeded." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, on the dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard, do two things and then save: (1) Open dashboard settings (gear icon) -> General, and add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's Tags field, then save/apply the settings. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours (click the time range picker in the top bar and choose 'Last 6 hours'). Then click Save dashboard and confirm the save succeeded ('Dashboard saved' confirmation). Report the tags shown in dashboard settings and the time range shown in the top bar after saving." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, on the dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard, set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m': click the time range picker in the top bar, find the 'Auto refresh' / 'Refresh interval' dropdown (bottom of the time range popover), and select '1m'. Then click Save dashboard, make sure the 'Update default time range' checkbox is checked in the save dialog, and confirm the save succeeded ('Dashboard saved' confirmation). Report the auto-refresh interval value shown in the top bar after saving." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, do a final verification of the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard. Reload the page fresh (navigate to the URL without extra query params). Then report: (1) the dashboard title shown in the top bar; (2) the exact titles of all panels on the dashboard; (3) the time range shown in the top bar time picker; (4) the auto-refresh interval shown in the top bar; (5) open dashboard settings (gear icon) -> General and report the tags listed; (6) open the panel editor for the panel titled 'fwgr7-n1 Availability' and report which data source its query uses and which visualization type it is; (7) report the text content shown in the 'fwgr7-n1 Notes' panel. Do not change anything." --session fwgr7-n1 --json

finalText:
All objectives verified on a fresh page load. Final report:

**Objective 1 — DONE.** The provisioned dashboard `Service health` (URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/bench-service-health/service-health) contains 3 panels, titled exactly: **Request rate**, **Error count**, **Latency by endpoint**.

**Objective 2 — DONE.** New dashboard **fwgr7-n1 Bench Dashboard** created and saved, containing a **Stat** panel titled **fwgr7-n1 Availability** whose query uses the **TestData** data source (verified by reopening the panel editor after a fresh reload: data source = TestData, visualization = Stat).

**Objective 3 — DONE.** The same dashboard contains a **Text** panel titled **fwgr7-n1 Notes** whose rendered content is **"Notes for run fwgr7-n1"** (includes the runid). Saved.

**Objective 4 — DONE.** Dashboard settings → General shows the tag **bench**, and the top-bar time picker reads **Last 6 hours** (URL `from=now-6h&to=now`). Saved with "Update default time range" checked.

**Objective 5 — DONE.** The top-bar auto-refresh control reads **1m** (URL `refresh=1m`). Saved with "Update default refresh value" checked.

**Objective 6 — DONE.** Dashboard URL: **http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/afwk79qhv4a9sf/fwgr7-n1-bench-dashboard** — UID: **afwk79qhv4a9sf**.

All changes were confirmed persisted by reloading the dashboard fresh (no query params) and re-reading the title, both panel titles, time range, refresh interval, tags, panel data source/visualization, and text content.
